content: The University of Worcester is located in Worcester, United Kingdom. It was officially granted university status by the Privy Council in September 2005. Prior to this, it was known as University College Worcester, and earlier as Worcester College of Higher Education. It is the only university serving the regions of Herefordshire and Worcestershire. The institution was originally established in 1947 as part of the University of Birmingham's Department of Education. It functioned as an Emergency Teacher Training College during its early years. In the 1970s, the Council for National Academic Awards (CNAA) began validating degrees for the Worcester College of Higher Education. In 1995, the Herefordshire and Worcestershire College of Nursing and Midwifery was integrated into the institution. By 1997, the Privy Council granted the institution the authority to award its own degrees, leading to its rebranding as University College Worcester (UCW). In 2005, it achieved full university status. In the same year, the university announced plans to construct a groundbreaking superlibrary in the center of Worcester. This facility would serve as a combined university and public library, marking the first of its kind in the United Kingdom. Additionally, a second campus was planned on the site of the former Worcester Royal Infirmary, located on Castle Street, with construction scheduled to begin in early 2007. The university also hosts a resident applied theatre company known as C&T. The Worcester Students' Union serves as the official student union for all individuals enrolled at the University of Worcester. It provides a variety of facilities and services, including a shop, offices, a bar named The Dive, a sandwich shop, a lounge area, a computer facility, a Student Advice Bureau, and a Student Development and Welfare Office.
